docs.title: CIV / UEE Risk
docs.text: Assessment of the knock-on risk the national UEE Training Package overhaul poses to the proposed 22697VIC CIV in Integrated Technologies (Electrotechnology stream) at Joondalup.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: • CIV/UEE Risk Summary — What's happening, unit-level exposure, timing, and what's not affected

docs.title: CIV (Electrotechnology) — UEE Training Package Knock-On Risk
What's happening
docs.text: The national UEE Electrotechnology Training Package is currently under a full review — 74 qualifications, 552 units, 75 skill sets — led by Powering Skills Organisation. Draft consultation opens May 2026.

docs.title: How the proposed CIV is exposed
docs.text:
The 22697VIC CIV, packaged with an Electrotechnology-stream elective set, requires exactly 6 units from that stream. Of those 6, 5 are national UEE units, not Victorian-specific:

Unit Content UEECD0007 WHS/OHS regulations UEECD0019 Fabricate/assemble utilities components UEECD0046 Solve problems in single-path circuits UEERL0003 In-service safety testing UEECD0052 Industry fundamentals — energy sector equipment

There is no spare capacity in this stream — exactly 6 slots, exactly 6 units selected. If any of these are superseded, merged, or deleted as part of the review, the qualification's packaging rules can't absorb it as-is.

docs.title: Why UEECD0007 specifically is a flashpoint
docs.text: This unit alone sits inside roughly 170 qualifications across 11 training packages nationally. Units with that much cross-package reach have a documented history of being contested and revised whenever a package review touches them — it's not a fringe unit that's unlikely to move.

docs.title: The timing problem
docs.text:
• CIV packaging finalised for 2026 delivery at Joondalup
  • Cohort starts Semester 1, 2026
  • UEE draft consultation opens May 2026 — mid-way through the first delivery period
  • If any of the 5 units are flagged for change, a formal packaging variation is required to keep delivering the CIV as currently structured — potentially while a cohort is partway through it

docs.title: What this doesn't affect
docs.text: The same qualification code (22697VIC) can also be packaged with a Robotics-stream elective set instead. That packaging draws only on Victorian-coded and Manufacturing-package (MEM) units — none from the UEE package — so it carries none of this exposure. The risk is specific to the Electrotechnology-stream packaging, not the qualification as a whole.

docs.title: Timeline: CIV vs UEE overhaul
docs.text:
timeline
    title CIV (22697VIC, Electrotechnology stream) vs UEE Training Package Overhaul
    2025 Q4 : CIV packaging finalised for Joondalup, 2026 delivery
    2026 Sem 1 : CIV launches with first cohort
    2026 May : UEE draft consultation opens — 5 of 6 Electrotechnology electives potentially exposed
    2026 Sem 2 : Possible supersession mid-cohort — packaging variation required to keep delivering as-is
